title: The Blast Window
subtitle: Quarry blasting cracks houses; the quarry employs the people whose walls are cracking
coldOpen: 11:00. A quarry blast cracks a wall in the records lane.
Half the lane works at the quarry.

briefing.grievance: Residents say the blasts have grown stronger for a month and now their walls are cracking. The quarry says the blasts are within the permit. Both sides are the same families.
knownFacts: The quarry permit limits charge size and blast hours.
Three houses show fresh cracks; one wall has shifted.
Two hundred lane residents work at the quarry.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the quarry uses double charges at lunch.
A message says the collector owns a share in the quarry.
briefing.responsibility: You run the mines and safety desk for the district. The lane needs its walls; it also needs its wages.
briefing.objective: Measure the blasts, make the houses safe, and keep the quarry working within its permit.

rightsMoments.question: Two houses are unsafe. The families refuse to leave, fearing they will never return. What does a fair safety order look like?

options.text: Notice, a reason, temporary housing nearby, and a written right to return once repairs are done.
options.feedback: Correct. Safety powers must still follow due process and leave a route home.

options.text: Carry them out; safety overrides everything, including notice.
options.feedback: Forced removal without notice or a route back turns protection into eviction.

options.text: Do nothing; their house, their risk.
options.feedback: The state has a duty to protect life, and it can be met with lawful, humane measures.

rightsMoments.principle: The right to shelter and to life (Article 21) means safety orders need notice, reasons, alternatives and a right to return, not just a decision to clear.
rightsMoments.why: Two flats and a written return date moved the families; a forced evacuation would have fulfilled their fear.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: Two houses are unsafe. The families fear they will never come back. What is a fair safety order?

options.a: Notice, a reason, a nearby place to stay, and a written right to return.
options.b: Carry them out. Safety beats everything.
options.c: Do nothing. Their house, their risk.

feedback.a: Yes! Safety still needs fairness and a way home.
feedback.b: No. Removing people with no way back is eviction.
feedback.c: The state must protect life, fairly.

simple.principle: A safety order needs notice, a reason, a place to stay and a way back home.
simple.why: Two flats and a return date moved the families. Force would have proved their fear right.
